props.title: Jane Eyre
props.initialSlug: Gothic romance of an orphan's forbidden love

sections.content: Orson Welles and Joan Fontaine bring Gothic intensity to Robert Stevenson's Jane Eyre, a defining adaptation that influenced decades of brooding period romances. The film's expressionistic shadows and Bernard Herrmann's haunting score established a template for portraying Victorian literary adaptations on screen. This version particularly influenced later Gothic romances like Rebecca (1940) and Dragonwyck (1946), while its psychological complexity paved the way for Great Expectations (1946) and subsequent Dickens adaptations. movies.title: Jane Eyre
movies.slug: Orson Welles and Joan Fontaine star in this Gothic adaptation of Charlotte Brontë's novel, featuring moody cinematography and a memorable Bernard Herrmann score

sections.content: The film's visual style draws heavily from German Expressionism, with cinematographer George Barnes creating stark contrasts and ominous shadows that would influence horror-tinged romances for years to come. This approach is particularly evident in Thornfield Hall's forbidding architecture and the memorable fire sequence. Gaslight (1944) and The Spiral Staircase (1946) would later employ similar techniques to create psychological tension in Victorian settings.

The film's treatment of childhood trauma and religious hypocrisy was groundbreaking for 1943, especially in the Lowood School sequences. This psychological depth influenced later literary adaptations like Great Expectations (1946) and Wuthering Heights (1939), while establishing a pattern for exploring complex themes within period settings. sections.content: Stevenson's adaptation crystallized many elements that became standard in Gothic romance films: the brooding male lead, the innocent but strong-willed heroine, and architectural spaces that reflect psychological states. These elements echo through later works like The Innocents (1961) and The Haunting (1963), showing how Jane Eyre helped establish the visual language of Gothic cinema.
